source_identity_policy: IDs are stable within this stage. Later plan-driven sources, if needed, must be appended under new IDs; existing IDs must not be rebound.

records.title: Automerge Rust core API
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0; docs.rs versioned page. Source commit not inspected.
records.locator: Automerge methods: apply_changes, save, get_heads, set_author; current crate page identifies 0.12.0.
records.review_method: Opened the Rust API documentation; no code executed.
records.observed_operation: apply_changes is idempotent for already-applied changes. save serializes the entirety of a document in compact form. An Author must be set; otherwise Change::author is None.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Idempotence applies to replaying identical changes. A missing author is allowed by default. save is a full-document save, not a transport or durable-write guarantee.
records.applicability: Directly applicable to a Rust+Slint client as the document core. The app still owns local crash-safe persistence, relay authentication, and mapping authenticated crew identities to author metadata.

records.title: Automerge Rust ReadDoc conflict and history API
records.locator: get_all/get_all_at at trait methods; *_at description and get_cursor methods.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned ReadDoc API page and read the relevant method declarations and descriptions.
records.observed_operation: get_all returns all values and operation IDs for a property; get_all_at and other *_at methods read a historical state at ChangeHash heads. get_cursor creates a stable address within a list or text sequence; movement policy handles a referenced item later being removed.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Historical reads need the chosen head set. A cursor addresses a sequence position, not a cue entity; if its referenced item is removed, the MoveCursor policy matters.
records.applicability: Use get_all for field-level conflict candidates and *_at for approved revision materialization. Cue-level comments should still store cue_id; cursors are only a possible optional text-range anchor.

records.title: Automerge Rust sync protocol
records.locator: Sync Protocol opening and example loop.
records.review_method: Opened the Rust sync module documentation; no messages were sent.
records.observed_operation: Each peer maintains a State per peer. The initiator generates the first message, the receiver applies it and generates a reply, and peers exchange messages until neither generates another.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The documented protocol assumes a reliable in-order stream. This is a protocol requirement; after possible loss, the prior state is unsafe to reuse without recovery.
records.applicability: A WebSocket/TCP relay can provide ordered delivery within a connection, but the app must detect disconnect uncertainty and reset/reconcile session state. The reference loop is guidance, not a tested relay.

records.title: Automerge Rust sync State
records.locator: State::encode/decode, new_read_only, read_only and set_read_only descriptions.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned Rust sync State page.
records.observed_operation: State can be encoded and decoded for reuse with the same peer. A read-only State ignores incoming changes while continuing to send its local changes.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Read-only is directional protocol behavior, not a data-store ACL. Persist state only while the peer/session relationship remains valid; if a message could have been lost, issue #1284 and the maintainer require reset.
records.applicability: Can help construct a publish-only client/relay path, but approval records and relay authorization must be separately enforced.

records.title: Rust sync lost-message issue #1284
records.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-02-13; no target crate version named in the issue. Open, no assignee or linked fix/PR visible at 2026-10-12T01:05:53Z.
records.locator: Issue reproduction steps for offline-generated message and reconnect (lines 243–268); maintainer reply (lines 273–284).
records.review_method: Opened the primary repository issue and read the reproducer and maintainer response.
records.observed_operation: Reporter demonstrates that generating then dropping an unsent sync message before an offline conflicting edit can make reconnect synchronization loop indefinitely; keeping the exact unsent message avoids that reproduction. Maintainer says the protocol requires reliable in-order delivery and sync state must be reset if a message may have been dropped.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue is open; it is not evidence that every release fails or that JavaScript has the same behavior. The maintainer explains the required recovery contract but does not supply an application relay implementation.
records.applicability: Direct Rust reconnect risk. Persist local document first; on uncertain disconnect reset/rebuild sync State or preserve the exact in-flight message/state pair; test the reproduction against the selected crate and adapter.

records.title: Automerge conflict behavior (language-neutral behavior described in JS docs)
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation, accessed 2026-10-12. Rust API cross-check is S02 (0.12.0).
records.locator: Concurrent map assignment example and explanation of getConflicts / multi-value register.
records.review_method: Opened the official Automerge conflict guide.
records.observed_operation: Independent edits to different fields combine. Concurrent writes to one property expose a deterministic visible winner and retain all values for a conflict query. Winner ordering is operation-ID based, not wall-clock latest.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This page uses the JavaScript getConflicts name and is not Rust API syntax; Rust get_all is documented separately. A later causally dependent assignment resolves the prior property conflict.
records.applicability: Supports a human decision panel for same-field candidates, provided Rust UI uses get_all and explicitly records a user resolution rather than presenting the deterministic winner as approval.

records.title: Automerge collaborative text behavior
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation; code examples are JavaScript.
records.locator: Collaborative text editing, splice/updateText, frequency caveat.
records.review_method: Opened the official Automerge text guide.
records.observed_operation: Collaborative strings are text sequences. Fine-grained splice edits merge concurrently; updateText can derive changes from a full input value but works best when called frequently, while less frequent whole-value diffs may merge poorly.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a JavaScript UI guide. The native Rust text transaction/update methods and Slint event mapping must be confirmed before implementation.
records.applicability: Cue notes/comments need actual text operations, not blind whole-value replacements. Even a converged text sequence may need a human readability review for overlapping/offline replacements.

records.title: Automerge fine-grained lists and history/size guidance
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current project documentation; current page reviewed 2026-10-12. Related history/performance locator: https://automerge.org/docs/cookbook/modeling-data/.
records.locator: List guide entity-map + ID-list pattern (around lines 116–134); Modeling Data Performance section (around lines 163–168).
records.review_method: Opened the official list and data-modeling guides.
records.observed_operation: The docs advise updating fine-grained entity fields and ID lists instead of replacing an entire nested object. Documents keep their entire change history by default, and the docs recommend workload-specific measurements.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The list examples are JavaScript but illustrate Automerge's data model. History retention means deleted values may remain in the document history unless a separate retention/compaction policy is established.
records.applicability: Store cue objects by stable ID and order IDs separately. Unknown cue counts require a later storage/load/sync benchmark and explicit privacy/history retention policy.

records.title: Move-aware JSON CRDT research
records.released_version_or_commit: Da and Kleppmann, arXiv v2 last revised 2024-03-19; PaPoC 2024 paper, DOI 10.1145/3642976.3653030. Research publication, not a crate release.
records.locator: Abstract and introduction: concurrent moves, duplicate/cycle hazard, proposed algorithm and planned Automerge integration.
records.review_method: Opened the primary paper record/version and inspected the original paper result.
records.observed_operation: The paper introduces a move operation for JSON CRDTs to handle concurrent move/non-move edits, and explicitly describes the algorithm as planned for Automerge integration.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a research algorithm, not evidence of an Automerge release/API. The scope includes maps/lists and concurrent tree interactions; application-specific semantics still require testing.
records.applicability: Relevant to cue reorder anomalies. Treat as design evidence motivating explicit same-cue move decisions, not as a selectable shipped library feature.

records.title: Automerge merge rules for list operations
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current Automerge project documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
records.locator: List merge rules, especially item IDs/references and caveat on reverse multi-item insertion.
records.review_method: Opened the official merge-rules page; cross-checked against the move paper.
records.observed_operation: List writes/deletes refer to element IDs and inserts to a predecessor element; concurrent inserts are deterministically ordered. The docs describe cases where insertion order is not preserved (especially reverse insertion).
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The page explains list operations, not a high-level atomic move command. Its JavaScript examples do not replace Rust API/version checks.
records.applicability: A reorder action cannot assume list CRDT order always equals intent. Record move intent and detect same-cue concurrent destinations; preserve both for review.

records.title: Yrs release history
records.released_version_or_commit: v0.28.0 released 2026-09-17 at commit 23b7f56; v0.27.3 commit ac476a4.
records.locator: v0.28.0 release record and v0.27.3 fixes.
records.review_method: Opened the primary Yrs release list.
records.observed_operation: v0.27.3 fixed inserting at index 0 missing the right-side neighbor and sticky-index right association. v0.28.0 is the later release (commit 23b7f56).
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The v0.27.3 bug fix is version-specific historical evidence; v0.28.0 is later. It does not establish absence of other ordering bugs.
records.applicability: Insertion-at-head and stable-anchor regressions deserve explicit boundary tests if Yrs is chosen; pin the release rather than relying on an unversioned docs page.

records.title: Yrs Rust update application
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate yrs 0.28.0; release commit recorded at S11.
records.locator: encode_update and apply_update; duplicate-block and pending-update descriptions.
records.review_method: Opened the docs.rs page, confirmed its header says yrs 0.28.0, and read update methods.
records.observed_operation: Document updates are idempotent and commutative; duplicate blocks are ignored; out-of-order updates whose predecessors are absent are stashed until prerequisites arrive.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: All replicas still need the same updates eventually. Stashing does not recover a permanently lost update without retry/reconciliation.
records.applicability: Strong alternative for retry/out-of-order binary updates in a Rust app, but does not itself expose the app-specific human conflict queue or publication boundary.

records.title: Yrs document, map conflicts, and shared types
records.locator: Document sync examples and Other shared types: ClientID uniqueness, ArrayRef/MapRef behavior.
records.review_method: Opened the docs.rs crate page, confirmed version 0.28.0, and inspected the root documentation.
records.observed_operation: The doc describes StateVector/diff or update observers for peer synchronization. Client IDs must be unique per active peer. Array concurrent same-position insertions resolve in deterministic order; concurrent MapRef assignments prioritize higher ClientID.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Duplicate active client IDs can corrupt document state. The documented map rule says how a visible winner is chosen; it does not establish that the app has a human-facing loser/conflict workflow.
records.applicability: Use a unique persistent device/client identity if Yrs is selected. Add a separate conflict-intent representation/UI; don't equate deterministic tie-breaking with human review.

records.title: Yrs stable text anchors
records.locator: StickyIndex description, serialization traits, get_offset, empty-collection scope.
records.review_method: Opened the docs.rs page and confirmed version 0.28.0.
records.observed_operation: StickyIndex refers to a content block rather than a fixed numeric offset and can be encoded/serialized; the resolved offset changes when content is inserted before it.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: An empty collection has no block ID to reference, and a resolved offset is only valid at that current document state. It is a text/sequence anchor, not a cue's stable entity identity.
records.applicability: Useful only if comments are later anchored to a range inside text; cue-level comment records should use cue_id.

records.title: Yjs shared-type movement caveat
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official Yjs documentation; access date 2026-10-12.
records.locator: Caveats section: integrated shared type cannot be moved to a different position.
records.review_method: Opened the official Yjs shared-types guide.
records.observed_operation: An integrated shared type cannot be integrated into another document position; copy it if another position is required.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This is the Yjs guide, not a standalone guarantee about every Yrs application API; Yrs 0.28.0 has its own preliminary/integrated type rules in S13.
records.applicability: Keep stable cue records separate from the order sequence; moving list entries should move IDs/placements rather than reuse a nested shared object.

records.title: Automerge Repo storage/network plumbing
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned current documentation; examples use @automerge/automerge-repo JavaScript packages.
records.locator: Repository entry point and StorageAdapter/NetworkAdapter example.
records.observed_operation: Repo composes local StorageAdapters with zero or more NetworkAdapters; the example uses a WebSocket server and filesystem adapter.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This documented Repo API is for JavaScript. The public tutorial relay is explicitly demo-only, not private or production reliable (Network Sync page).
records.applicability: Useful architecture precedent for separating storage and transport, but does not remove the need for Rust storage/relay implementation and does not authorize a public demo server for rehearsal data.

records.title: Automerge sync handshake documentation correction, issue #945
records.released_version_or_commit: JavaScript issue filed against @automerge/automerge 2.2.4, reproduced on 2.2.8; closed; collaborator response 2024-08-23.
records.locator: Collaborator response correcting receiveSyncMessage documentation; working send/receive loop.
records.observed_operation: The receiver must call generateSyncMessage after receiveSyncMessage to decide whether a response remains; the old docs mistakenly implied receive returned a new message. A working loop was posted and confirmed.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This was a JavaScript API/docs mismatch, not proof of a current Rust API defect. Rust 0.12.0's sync module provides its own current typed example.
records.applicability: Historical warning for hand-written protocol adapters: implement and test the exact native-version handshake instead of porting stale examples.
